topic: Mastering Limits: From Visual Intuition to Analytical Precision

sections.title: Intuitive Foundation: The Concept of 'Getting Closer'
sections.content: Define limits as the behavior of a function as x approaches a point, regardless of the value at the point. Use a graphical animation of a 'Robot Vacuum' navigating toward a charger (the limit point) to illustrate convergence without necessarily reaching the target.
sections.example: Visualizing f(x) = (x^2-1)/(x-1) as x approaches 1; the hole at x=1 is bypassed by the 'Robot Vacuum' approaching from both sides.

sections.title: Formal Rigor: The Epsilon-Delta Definition
sections.content: Transition from intuition to analytical proof. Explain that for any tiny error range (epsilon) around the limit, there exists a distance (delta) such that all inputs fall within the target. Use a 'Target Practice' animation where narrowing the scope (epsilon) forces a tighter required accuracy of input (delta).
sections.example: Proving lim(2x+1) = 5 as x -> 2: If we want to be within 0.1 of 5, how close (delta) must x be to 2? (Result: |x-2| < 0.05).

sections.title: Computational Shortcut: L'Hôpital's Rule
sections.content: Introduce L'Hôpital's Rule as a tool for indeterminate forms (0/0 or ∞/∞). Explain the prerequisite: the functions must be differentiable. Show an animation where the slopes of two competing curves determine the limit of their ratio.
sections.example: Calculating lim(x->0) sin(x)/x. Show how taking derivatives of numerator and denominator reveals the limit is 1, visually matching the slope of sin(x) at the origin.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Briefly recap the logic flow: Intuition (The Goal) -> Epsilon-Delta (The Proof) -> L'Hôpital (The Calculation). Emphasize that while L'Hôpital is powerful for computation, Epsilon-Delta is the foundation of calculus logic.
sections.example: A quick 'Quiz Dash' animation: Identify when to use the definition (theory) versus L'Hôpital (solving a complex limit like lim(x->0) (e^x-1)/x).
